frontier.hypothesis: candidate.c's F1 chain-extender is now the ONLY unsanctioned-looking construct in a floor-1 body, and s16 proves target's own source carried a construct of exactly that class -- so the decidable question is whether the annotated F1 form is acceptable, or whether a sixth stptr reference exists in some spelling that survives cse2.
frontier.mechanism: reg_n_refs frozen pre-combine (flow.c:2081, combine.c:55-56) vs reg_live_length recomputed post-combine (sched.c:5106) makes a combine-deleted reference free in live range; combine deletes an insn only by folding it into its consumer within one basic block, so a sixth stptr-referencing insn is structurally a constant-offset chain step -- i.e. an F1 construct by shape, whatever it is called.

frontier.hypothesis: loop1 emits 43 asm insns from 40 sched1-era RTL insns, so three of loop1's emitted insns are created after sched1 (by reload). If a source form moved one MORE loop1 insn across that boundary, stptr's live length would drop to 40 with the bytes unchanged -- the only surviving loophole in the live-40 kill.
frontier.mechanism: sched1 accumulates reg_live_length over its own scheduled list (sched.c:3165/5106), which does not yet contain reload-generated insns; the emitted count is what the scorer sees.
